samples.summary: New worksheet-images tab gate uses the bare truthiness check the repo already documents as bypassable via Yorkie proxy magic keys
samples.evidence: `worksheetOrThrow` (worksheet-images.controller.ts:57-58) resolves the caller-controlled `:tabId` path segment with `const worksheet = root.sheets?.[tabId]; if (!worksheet) throw NotFound`. The sibling controller `worksheet-structure.controller.ts:83-116` documents that this is not sufficient: `root.sheets` is a Yorkie `JSONObject` proxy whose get trap answers `getID` / `toJSON` / `toJS` / `toJSForTest` / `toString` with a **function** — truthy — and its spec pins that exact vector (`worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:229-251` asserts NotFound for `toString`, `toJSON`, `toJS`, `toJSForTest`, `getID`, `__proto__`, `constructor`). It fixes it with `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(sheets).includes(tabId)`; the new controller does not use that helper. Attack: `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/<ws>/documents/<sheetDoc>/tabs/toString/images` with a valid write-scoped key walks past the tab gate at line 106 and again at line 108, then line 111-112 executes `ws.images = {}` / `ws.images[id] = image` against the trap's bound function instead of a worksheet — the request answers 200 with `{images}` for a write that landed nowhere. On a plain-object root (`tabId=__proto__`) the same two lines resolve to `Object.prototype` and assign `images` onto it, which is process-wide prototype pollution. The same bare pattern is repeated in the new comments controller at comments.controller.ts:323-326 for the body-supplied `tabId` (it only fails closed by accident, because `worksheet.rowOrder` is undefined on a function). I confirmed the proxy behaviour only from the sibling controller's own docblock and spec, not by executing against a live Yorkie, hence medium confidence.

samples.summary: parseImages stores an arbitrary attacker-chosen `src` URL with no scheme or origin validation
samples.evidence: `parseImage` (worksheet-images.ts:51) accepts `src` through `requireString` only — any scheme, any host. The stored value is written verbatim into the CRDT (worksheet-images.controller.ts:112) and every viewer of that spreadsheet, including anonymous share-link viewers, renders it as an `` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-object-layer.tsx:216 with the raw-ish `resolveImageSrc(image.src)`). So a caller with a write-scoped key can plant `https://attacker.example/px.png` (or a `data:` payload) on a tab and receive a request — IP, User-Agent, timing — from every person who opens the document, i.e. a stored tracking/beacon primitive against workspace members and share-link recipients. The backend already owns the origin rule this endpoint skips: `document/document-image-refs.ts#parseImageRef` refuses foreign-origin and protocol-relative image URLs (see its spec at document-image-refs.spec.ts:26-48), and the frontend calls the equivalent check "a SECURITY boundary" that exists because "`data.src` comes from the CRDT and a malicious collaborator can set it" (packages/frontend/src/api/share-image-url.ts:18-27). Neither rule is applied on this new write path. Searched: parseImages/parseImage in packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-images.ts, all `src` handling in the controller, grep for isTrustedWorkspaceImageUrl / parseImageRef / isRehostable across packages, and the frontend render path (image-object-layer.tsx, image-cache.ts) — found no scheme or origin check on this route.

samples.summary: API comment routes create notifications by calling the service directly, bypassing the per-user throttle that guards the equivalent HTTP endpoint
samples.evidence: `notify()` calls `this.notificationService.createFromComment(actorId, plan)` (comments.controller.ts:206) directly. The only other caller, `POST /notifications/comment`, is deliberately guarded by `@UseGuards(UserThrottlerGuard)` + `@Throttle({ ttl: 60_000, limit: 30 })` (notification.controller.ts:63-65) precisely because it is "the one endpoint a client can call on its own initiative", and `UserThrottlerGuard` exists because IP keying "leaves an attacker with several source addresses effectively uncapped" (user-throttler.guard.ts:7-11). The new path inherits only the global 120/min **per-IP** bucket (app.module.ts:97-104), so one workspace member with a write-scoped key can create ~4x more notification rows per minute than the browser path, keyed on address rather than on the user — the exact property UserThrottlerGuard was written to remove. Each request fans out to `MAX_RECIPIENTS` (20) members with a fresh `commentId` dedupe key, so nothing absorbs the repeats. docs/design/notifications.md acknowledges the omission but justifies it as "bounded by the one-comment-per-request shape", which the per-IP-only limit does not enforce per user.

samples.summary: No length bound on a comment body written through the API
samples.evidence: `normalizeBody` (comment-ops.ts, the `raw.trim().length > 0 ? raw : null` check) validates type and emptiness only, and it is the sole validation on `body` for `POST /comments`, `POST /comments/:id/replies` and `PATCH /comments/:id/comments/:id` (comments.controller.ts:269, 354, 416). `@Body() body: unknown` means the global ValidationPipe does not apply (no DTO metatype), so the only remaining bound is `bodyParser.json({ limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT })` in main.ts:49. A write-scoped key can therefore persist a multi-megabyte comment body into the Yorkie CRDT, where it is replicated to every connected editor of that document on open — a cheap, persistent resource-exhaustion write. The notification DTO caps its `preview` at 2000 chars (notification.dto.ts:66) and the service truncates to 200, so the sibling surface bounds its input while this one does not. Searched: normalizeBody in yorkie/comment-ops.ts, all three body validation sites in comments.controller.ts, the sheets engine's assertNonEmpty rule, notification.dto.ts limits, and main.ts body-parser configuration — no MaxLength equivalent anywhere on this path.

samples.summary: Caller-controlled image `id` is used as an object key with no rejection of `__proto__` / `constructor`
samples.evidence: `for (const image of images) ws.images[image.id] = image` (worksheet-images.controller.ts:112) keys the collection by a value `parseImage` only requires to be a non-empty string (worksheet-images.ts:41-46, `requireString(i.id, 'id')`). A body of `{"images":[{"id":"__proto__", ...}]}` therefore performs `ws.images['__proto__'] = <object>`, which on a plain object is a prototype assignment rather than an own property, and `constructor` / `prototype` are equally reachable. The repo treats this key class as a real hazard elsewhere and rejects it explicitly (yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:117 rejects a `__proto__` merge key, with worksheet-settings.spec.ts:90 building the body via `JSON.parse` because that is "the shape that matters"). Whether it is exploitable here depends on the Yorkie object proxy's set trap, which I could not execute, so confidence is low; the missing validation itself is plain. Searched: parseImage/parseImages in yorkie/worksheet-images.ts, the assignment sites in worksheet-images.controller.ts, and grep for `__proto__` guards across packages/backend/src (only worksheet-settings.ts and worksheet-structure.controller.ts guard it).

verdict.reason: Evidence verified as described. worksheet-images.controller.ts:53-60 does use the bare `const worksheet = root.sheets?.[tabId]; if (!worksheet) throw NotFound` on a caller-controlled `:tabId` path segment (controller prefix at line 32), and that lookup feeds the writes at lines 106-112 (`ws.images = {}`, `ws.images[image.id] = image`) plus the raw read at line 72. The sibling worksheet-structure.controller.ts:83-116 documents this exact bypass (Yorkie proxy get trap answers getID/toJSON/toJS/toJSForTest/toString with a truthy function; __proto__/constructor truthy on plain objects) and fixes it with `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(sheets).includes(tabId)` at line 112; the helper exists (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:33) and is exported (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:169) but is not used by the images controller. The repo pins the vector in a regression spec (worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:229-251) with no equivalent case in worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts. Route guards (line 33: CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard) and assertSheetDocument (lines 40-51) constrain auth and document type only — nothing validates tabId, so no already-guarded refutation applies. The repeated pattern in comments.controller.ts:323-326 (body-supplied tabId, then `root.sheets[tabId]` at line 330) is also present as claimed. In lane as unsafe input handling / property-key injection on a write path; not refutable.

finding.summary: parseImages stores an arbitrary attacker-chosen `src` URL with no scheme or origin validation
finding.evidence: `parseImage` (worksheet-images.ts:51) accepts `src` through `requireString` only — any scheme, any host. The stored value is written verbatim into the CRDT (worksheet-images.controller.ts:112) and every viewer of that spreadsheet, including anonymous share-link viewers, renders it as an `` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-object-layer.tsx:216 with the raw-ish `resolveImageSrc(image.src)`). So a caller with a write-scoped key can plant `https://attacker.example/px.png` (or a `data:` payload) on a tab and receive a request — IP, User-Agent, timing — from every person who opens the document, i.e. a stored tracking/beacon primitive against workspace members and share-link recipients. The backend already owns the origin rule this endpoint skips: `document/document-image-refs.ts#parseImageRef` refuses foreign-origin and protocol-relative image URLs (see its spec at document-image-refs.spec.ts:26-48), and the frontend calls the equivalent check "a SECURITY boundary" that exists because "`data.src` comes from the CRDT and a malicious collaborator can set it" (packages/frontend/src/api/share-image-url.ts:18-27). Searched: parseImages/parseImage in packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-images.ts, all `src` handling in the controller, grep for isTrustedWorkspaceImageUrl / parseImageRef / isRehostable across packages, and the frontend render path (image-object-layer.tsx, image-cache.ts) — found no scheme or origin check on this route.

verdict.reason: The absence itself is real — parseImage validates `src` only via requireString (worksheet-images.ts:53-73), the controller stores it verbatim (worksheet-images.controller.ts:111-112), `@Body() body: unknown` bypasses the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65), and no img-src CSP exists (docs/design/notes/notes.md:623 says so explicitly). But it is not a blocking security defect under this lens. (1) No privilege boundary is crossed: the same CRDT field is written directly by every collaborator's Yorkie client with no server mediation (frontend sheet-view.tsx:549-551 sets ws.images[id].src inside doc.update), and the endpoint's guards (worksheet-images.controller.ts:33) demand the same workspace write authorization, so a write-scoped caller gains no capability they lacked. The repo states this threat model itself (document-image-refs.ts:53-58: "the string comes out of the CRDT, where any collaborator can write https://attacker.example/…") and mitigates at consumption. (2) The security-sensitive consequence — leaking a viewer's share token to a foreign host — is already blocked by the origin gate in share-image-url.ts:27-42 and :55-57. (3) Foreign-origin image src is deliberate shipped behaviour, not prohibited content: docs/image-insert.ts:80-107 stores a user-typed external https hotlink "as-is" with only a scheme check, and image-cache.ts:86-90 is written to expect third-party hosts. `` executes neither javascript: nor script inside data:image/svg+xml, so there is no XSS or exfiltration chain; residual impact is viewer IP/UA disclosure by an already-authorized editor, i.e. a defence-in-depth allow-list (minor/nit), not a major weakness.
